common_name: Karley Rose Fountain Grass (Vivid Rose-Pink Ornamental Grass)

planting.note: Divide clumps or plant container-grown starts in spring in full sun and well-drained, average to lean soil; Karley Rose is a sterile hybrid selection, so it must be propagated by division rather than seed and does not seed around the garden.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun, allowing room for the vigorous, mounding clump to fill in over its first two seasons. Karley Rose is the most widely planted selection of oriental fountain grass, prized for larger, more numerous, and more intensely rose-pink flower spikes than the species, held well above the fine-textured gray-green foliage from early summer into fall and glowing when backlit by low sun. It is more heat- and humidity-tolerant than many fountain grasses, performs reliably in the Gulf South, and, as a sterile hybrid, spreads only by clump expansion rather than self-seeding, making it a tidier choice than seed-grown fountain grasses for formal or mixed borders. Cut the clump back to a few inches in late winter before new growth emerges, and divide every three to four years if the center begins to die out.
